# `muya` (claude-control-plane) — System Documentation

**Last updated:** 2026-07-24
**Generated by:** spec-first-feature Phase 1 (refresh — supersedes the 2026-06-16 prototype-era doc)
**Status:** Current (post-migration)

> **Supersedes prototype doc.** The prior SYSTEM.md described the app as "only a UI prototype in `_prototype_ref/`, real product not yet written." That is obsolete. The native Tauri v2 + React desktop app is now fully built: React/TS frontend in `src/`, Rust core in `src-tauri/src/` (15 modules). This refresh documents the current code and is focused on the subsystems the SSH-config + CyberArk feature touches; a few non-feature modules are summarized from their header docs. Every architectural claim carries a `file:line` cite; unverified claims are marked `OPEN QUESTION`.

## 1. Overview

Muya is a native macOS (Apple Silicon) desktop control panel for running and observing multiple Claude Code sessions from one screen. It ships as a signed + notarized Tauri v2 app (releases v0.2.x). Unlike the old prototype, all data is real: live PTY terminals, scoped filesystem reads, git/PM status, Claude Code session/transcript readers, and a Claude-to-Claude remote bridge.

## 2. Architecture

Two layers:
- **Frontend** — React 19 + TypeScript SPA rendered in the Tauri webview. Monolithic shell/router in `src/App.tsx` (~113 KB) plus focused page/panel components under `src/components/`.
- **Rust core** — `src-tauri/src/`, 15 modules, exposing **31 `#[tauri::command]` functions** registered in one handler list (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:160` `tauri::generate_handler![...]`). Shared state registered via `.manage(...)` (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:153-159`).

Rust modules (purpose from module header docs):
| Module | Purpose (cite) |
|---|---|
| `agents.rs` | Claude Code session reader — shells `claude agents --json`, maps to frontend `AgentSession` (`agents.rs:1`) |
| `history.rs` | Session history reader — scans `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl` transcripts (`history.rs:1`) |
| `pty.rs` | PTY/terminal spawn + IO over `portable-pty` (`pty.rs:1`, `pty_spawn` `:46`) |
| `fs.rs` | Scoped, read-only workspace filesystem reads; owns its own security check (`fs.rs:1`); uses `reqwest` (`fs.rs:809,913`) |
| `pm.rs` | Project Manager — stateless git status + push/merge queue checks, derived live from `git` (`pm.rs:1`) |
| `watcher.rs` | Debounced filesystem watching → emits `fs-changed` Tauri event (`watcher.rs:1`) |
| `metrics.rs` | Live resource usage of THIS app process (`metrics.rs:1`) |
| `vault.rs` | Vault MCP integration — manages a persistent Python smart-connections subprocess, routes `vault_search` over JSON-RPC (`vault.rs:1`) |
| `bridge.rs`, `bridge_exec.rs`, `bridge_remote.rs` | Claude-to-Claude Remote Bridge — mTLS + SPAKE2 pairing, remote exec (`bridge_remote.rs:1`, ADR 0002) |
| `validate.rs` | Input validation (e.g. git URL) (`validate.rs:43`) |
| `lib.rs`, `main.rs`, `testutil.rs` | App entry, command registry, test helpers |

## 3. Services and Workers

No separate backend server. Long-running pieces run in-process:
- **PTY sessions** — spawned via `portable-pty` `native_pty_system().openpty()` (`pty.rs:63`); each is an interactive shell/command with a reader thread.
- **Filesystem watcher** — background debounced watcher emitting `fs-changed` (`watcher.rs:1`).
- **Vault MCP subprocess** — a persistent Python smart-connections process managed by `vault.rs`, spoken to over JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout.
- **Remote bridge listener** — mTLS server for Claude-to-Claude bridge (`bridge_remote.rs`).

## 4. Data Model & Persistence

- **Frontend UI prefs:** `localStorage` (`src/App.tsx:352-360`, keys `muya.leftWidth`, `apex.theme`, `apex.openTabs`).
- **Backend config: plain JSON files on disk** under `~/.claude/`. Canonical pattern in `vault.rs`: `~/.claude/muya-vault-config.json`, `load_config`/`save_config` (`vault.rs:79`, `:87-110`) via `serde_json`; config dir resolved with `dirs-next`.
- **No database.** State is either derived live (git/PM, agents, metrics) or read from `~/.claude` files owned by Claude Code (roster, jobs, transcripts).
- **Secrets at rest — see §9.** There is currently **no encrypted store and no OS Keychain usage**.

## 5. Rust Command Surface

Commands are plain `async fn` annotated `#[tauri::command]`, listed once in `generate_handler!` (`lib.rs:160`). Representative: `vault_get_status` (`vault.rs:283`). Distribution: `bridge_remote` (10), `bridge_exec` (6), `vault` (5), `pty` (4), `bridge` (4), `watcher` (1), plus reader modules. **To add a new subsystem:** create a module, add its commands to the `generate_handler!` list, and (if it holds state) `.manage(...)` it in `lib.rs`.

## 6. Frontend

- **Framework:** React 19 + TypeScript, Vite build, rendered in the Tauri webview.
- **View / page routing (THIS is where a new page plugs in):**
  - Top-level view state: `src/App.tsx:345` — `useState<"control"|"sessions"|"queue"|"tools"|"prd">("control")`.
  - Nav tab buttons: `src/App.tsx:1313-1359` (one `<button onClick={() => setView("...")}>` per tab).
  - Render switch: `src/App.tsx:1455-1495` — `view === "sessions"` → `SessionsPage` (`:1455`), `tools` → `ResourcesPage` (`:1464`), `queue` → `QueuePage` (`:1472`), `prd` → `PrdBoard` (`:1482`). `"control"` is **always mounted** and merely hidden via CSS (`:1495`) — a deliberate choice so the PTY/terminal is never unmounted (see §13, L1).
  - **Adding a view =** extend the union (`:345`), add a nav button (~`:1359`), add a `{view === "ssh" && <SshPage/>}` block (~`:1490`), import the component (`src/App.tsx:56-62`).
- **Config UI convention:** per-feature panels/modals, not a global settings page. Reference: `src/components/VaultConfigPanel.tsx` — `open` state, reads via `invoke("vault_get_status")`, persists via `invoke("vault_set_path")` + `invoke("vault_restart")`.
- **Frontend ↔ Rust:** `@tauri-apps/api` `invoke(name, args)`; events via `listen(...)`.
- **Terminal:** `src/components/Terminal.tsx` (xterm) ↔ `pty.rs`. Hidden terminals must re-fit + `focus()` on show (§13, L3).
- **Components** under `src/components/`: `SessionsPage`, `QueuePage`, `ResourcesPage`, `PrdBoard`, `SessionsPanel`, `VaultConfigPanel`, `SessionMonitor`, `Terminal`, `TerminalGrid`, `FileTree`, `FileEditor`, `ChatView`, `BranchDAG`, `MarkdownViewer`, `NewAgentModal`, `CreateWithClaudeModal`, `ScheduledPromptModal`.

## 7. Integrations

- **Claude Code (file/CLI):** `claude agents --json` (`agents.rs`), `~/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl` transcripts (`history.rs`), roster/jobs files.
- **Vault / smart-connections:** Python MCP subprocess for semantic search (`vault.rs`).
- **Remote bridge:** Claude-to-Claude over mTLS + SPAKE2 pairing (`bridge_remote.rs`, ADR 0002).
- **git:** live status/queue via `pm.rs`.
- **New (this feature):** CyberArk PAM REST API over HTTPS, and outbound `ssh` processes launched through the existing PTY.

## 8. Authentication & Authorization / Security Boundary

Single-machine, single-user personal tool — no user identity/login. The security boundary is **filesystem scope + local-only network**, not identity:
- `fs.rs` owns a manual scope check; reads are lazy + read-only (`fs.rs:1`).
- Remote bridge is mutually authenticated (mTLS) with SPAKE2 pairing PINs (`bridge_remote.rs`).
- Env-var secret **stripping** deny-list before spawning child processes (`bridge_exec.rs:60-86`).
- **Relevant to the SSH feature:** there is no existing credential/identity store — the new feature introduces the app's first at-rest secret storage, so it must bring its own crypto + Keychain integration.

## 9. Configuration & Secrets

- **Config:** plain JSON under `~/.claude/muya-*.json` (`vault.rs` pattern). Not encrypted (non-secret data only).
- **Certs/keys today:** the remote bridge writes cert/key material as **plain files with restricted permissions** via `write_secret_file` (`bridge_remote.rs:136`); identity keypair is Ed25519 via `rcgen`/`ring`.
- **Encryption-at-rest: NONE.** No `aes-gcm`, `argon2`, `zeroize`, `keyring`, or `security-framework` crate is present (verified in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`). Available today: `reqwest` 0.12 (rustls-tls), `rustls` 0.23, `tokio-rustls`, `serde`/`serde_json`, `dirs-next`, `rcgen`/`ring`, `sha2`, `hkdf`, `spake2-conflux`.
- **This is the exact gap the SSH-config feature fills:** an encrypted credential store + OS Keychain integration.

## 10. Deployment

Signed + notarized macOS (Apple Silicon) build. Release flow: `scripts/build-sign-notarize.sh` → `scripts/publish-release.sh` (requires a `CHANGELOG.md` `[x.y.z]` entry). Current line: v0.2.x. Notarization uses the `apex-notary` keychain profile; updater archive is `.app.tar.gz`.

## 11. Observability

Minimal — app-process metrics (`metrics.rs`) surfaced in the header telemetry. No external logging/tracing backend (local tool). Secrets must never reach logs (constraint for the new feature).

## 12. Key Design Decisions

- **Single always-mounted control view** — pages switch by CSS hide, not unmount, to keep PTY/terminal alive (`App.tsx:1495`; see L1).
- **Own the FS security check** — `fs.rs` uses raw `std::fs` instead of the Tauri fs plugin to control scope (`fs.rs:1`).
- **Stateless PM** — git facts derived live, no daemon (`pm.rs:1`).
- **Plain-JSON config** — simple, human-inspectable; acceptable because no secrets are stored today (§9). The new feature must NOT store secrets this way.

## 13. Known Constraints & Gotchas

- **L1 — PTY unmount kills the session:** never conditionally unmount stateful terminal components on view switch; keep mounted + `hidden` (`App.tsx:1495`).
- **L3 — hidden xterm resize/focus:** a hidden (0×0) terminal misses resizes; on show, re-fit + `pty_resize` + `term.focus()` in `requestAnimationFrame`.
- **React 19 StrictMode double-mount** — watch PTY/watcher subscriptions.
- **`App.tsx` is monolithic (~113 KB)** — new pages should be their own component files, not added inline.
- **No crypto/Keychain infra** — the SSH feature builds this from zero; get the primitives right (nonce uniqueness, Argon2 params, zeroization).

## 14. Open Questions

1. `OPEN QUESTION`: exact command count exposed to the frontend for reader modules (`agents.rs`/`fs.rs`/`history.rs`/`metrics.rs`/`pm.rs` did not match the `#[tauri::command]` grep — they may register commands via a different path or be called indirectly). Not blocking for the SSH feature.
2. `OPEN QUESTION`: whether the Tauri capability/permission config restricts outbound network (needed to confirm CyberArk HTTPS calls and `ssh` process spawn are allowed without a capability change).
